podcast.title: Country Folks (2013) - Rap and Country Audience Commonality
podcast.body: In 2013, Bubba Sparxxx released a posse cut with Colt Ford titled "Country Folks." This track explicitly highlighted the shared ground and commonality they perceived between rap and country music audiences. "A 2013 posse cut by Bubba and Colt called Country Folks laid bare the commonality they saw in rap and country audiences."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Collaborations with Country Artists
podcast.body: Bubba Sparxxx collaborated with other country rap artists, including Colt Ford, on songs that explored the commonalities between rap and country audiences. He is considered a "white country rap forebear." "He dropped bars alongside everyone from Country Mainstays, Jake Owen and Jason Aldin to his white country rap forebear, Bubba Sparks."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: Ride ’til I Can’t No More Edition Part 2

podcast.title: Pioneer in Genre Mixing
podcast.body: Bubba Sparxxx was among the artists who, decades prior to Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road," were mixing country music with R&B and Rap, contributing to a cross-genre tradition. "everyone from Ray Charles and the Rappen Duke to Bubba Sparks and Jason Aldine were mixing country music with R&B and Rapp."
